title: Conversion is intentional dealing with another's chattel inconsistent with possessory rights

content.overview: Conversion is intentional dealing with another's chattel inconsistent with possessory rights. Detinue historically concerned wrongful detention. A finder has qualified possessory rights subject to the true owner's superior claim.
content.glance: Conversion is intentional dealing with another's chattel inconsistent with possessory rights. Detinue historically concerned wrongful detention. A finder has qualified possessory rights subject to the true owner's superior claim.
content.study: Conversion is intentional dealing with another's chattel inconsistent with possessory rights. Detinue historically concerned wrongful detention. A finder has qualified possessory rights subject to the true owner's superior claim.\n\nThe law of goods distinguishes possession from ownership. Hollins v Fowler illustrates conversion; Armory v Delamirie illustrates a finder's possessory right against a stranger.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The law of goods distinguishes possession from ownership. Hollins v Fowler illustrates conversion; Armory v Delamirie illustrates a finder's possessory right against a stranger.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: The tort remains common-law, subject to statutes governing goods and transactions. Conversion can arise through taking, selling, destroying or otherwise exercising dominion inconsistent with another's rights.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Claimant has possessory or immediate right to possession. 2. Defendant intentionally deals with the chattel. 3. Dealing is inconsistent with claimant's rights. 4. Causation and loss are established.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Bills, invoices, possession records, photographs and valuation evidence may establish rights and quantum.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: The civil court may award damages, delivery or other appropriate relief. Limitation depends on the relief and applicable statute.

examples.title: Illustration 1 — Doctrine Satisfied
examples.body: A person with possessory rights can sue a stranger who wrongfully interferes with goods; a finder has qualified priority against strangers.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Defect
examples.body: A finder generally has qualified possessory rights, not absolute ownership against the true owner.
